_comment_database: Choose database provider: SqlServer (local SQL Server / SSMS on localhost) or Mongo (MongoDB). Default is SqlServer for local desktop database workflows.
_comment_mongo: Used when Database:Provider is set to 'Mongo' or for one-click migration from Mongo to SQL Server. The connection string is a SECRET and MUST stay empty here if sensitive. Supply it with 'dotnet user-secrets set "Mongo:ConnectionString" "..."' or the Mongo__ConnectionString environment variable.
_comment_admin: Controls access to administrative APIs. LocalOnly admits only a caller on this machine (suitable for local development and desktop use). Disabled switches administration off entirely.
_comment_encryption: Needed only to store AI provider keys through the admin console. A SECRET: supply it with 'dotnet user-secrets set "Encryption:DataKey" "..."' or Encryption__DataKey. Without it the app runs normally and the console says so instead of failing on save.
_comment_storage: DataRoot is the studio root: downloads, chunk jobs, thumbnails, logs and probe scratch are created inside it (a relative path resolves against the API project folder, never bin/). Durable media lives in LocalRoot: projects, uploaded assets, generated media and finished renders. FFmpeg render workspaces use Render:ScratchRoot. Switching Provider to S3 later is a config-only change; the app code is unchanged.
_comment_ffmpeg: An absolute path is strongly preferred: a service process's PATH is not the interactive shell's.

Ffmpeg._comment_merge_memory: A crossfade join names one ffmpeg input per clip, so every clip is opened at once and each decoder holds a frame pool sized by its thread count. Left unbounded that is where a long stitch dies: 24 clips at 1080p reached 2 GB of working set, and once the host starts paging the SAME join takes anywhere from 72s to 937s, which shows up as a render that randomly hits its timeout. MergeDecoderThreads caps each input's decoder (2 halves the memory at no cost in time - the output encoder is the bottleneck, and it is NOT capped). MaxMergeInputs is the backstop: beyond it the join is done as a cascade of smaller joins, which bounds memory at any clip count but costs one extra encode generation for the clips that pass through an intermediate level.

Render._comment_presets: Preset/Crf are the x264 settings for the DELIVERED video. IntermediatePreset is used instead for pass-one clip files in a stitch, which exist only to be re-encoded by the join and are then deleted - at a fixed CRF the preset buys compression efficiency rather than quality, so spending 'medium' on a throwaway file buys nothing. Set IntermediatePreset to the same value as Preset to opt out. A stitch with no transitions and no overlays stream-copies its clips instead of re-encoding them (music is mixed in without touching the video), and in that case Preset is used for them too.
Render._comment_speed: Preset/Crf apply to PROJECT renders. A clip export ignores them and uses the quality chosen in the export dialog instead - Fast (veryfast CRF 20), High (veryfast CRF 16, the default) or Best (medium CRF 14); see EncoderProfile.ForQuality for the measurements. ClipCacheRoot keeps conformed clips between exports (keyed by graph, inputs and encoder settings, so a different quality is a different entry), and a re-export only encodes the clips that changed - keep it on the same drive as ScratchRoot so entries are hard links instead of copies; empty disables it. UseHardwareEncoder sends throwaway intermediates to the GPU encoder the startup probe found; it is off because Quick Sync measured slower than libx264 here.
Render._comment_watermark: WatermarkText pre-fills the watermark box on the clip screen - put your site address here once, rather than typing it per video. WatermarkFontFile may stay EMPTY: the server finds a system font by itself at startup and logs which one it picked. Set it to an ABSOLUTE path to a .ttf/.otf to choose a different face - try C:/Windows/Fonts/segoeuib.ttf on Windows or /usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf on Linux. A text watermark is always drawn from a font FILE and never by family name: drawtext's font= resolves through fontconfig, and on a build with fontconfig but no fonts.conf (every stock Windows ffmpeg) the failed lookup CRASHES the renderer. If no font file can be found the watermark is skipped and the video is reported as completed with warnings.

_comment_liveStream: Go Live: a playlist (uploads, renders, assets, release kits, links) is first PREPARED - every item converted to the exact stream format, previewable - then SENT by copying the segments to the ingest, so sending costs little CPU and MaxConcurrentStreams is bounded by upload bandwidth, while MaxConcurrentPreparations bounds the x264 work. Callers choose a destination by id and never send a URL. Each IngestUrl must be rtmps:// - plain rtmp:// would send the stream key in clear text, so such entries are ignored. Keys are either pasted per stream (memory only) or saved per brand channel by an admin, encrypted with Encryption:DataKey and only ever shown masked; AllowSavedKeysForNonAdmins lets non-admins stream with saved keys. MaxHours ends even a 'loop until stopped' stream.
_comment_ingest: Paste and file upload always work. URL ingest needs YtDlp.Enabled AND the binary installed; downloading media needs the separate AllowMediaDownload gate as well.
_comment_ai: Every provider ships DISABLED. The app renders video with no AI at all - turn one on by setting Enabled:true and, where a key is needed, storing it through the admin API (never here). Chains are tried in order; the first configured, enabled, healthy provider wins, so a rate-limited free tier costs one skipped provider rather than a failed render.

lmstudio._comment: Model is left unset on purpose: LM Studio serves whichever model it has loaded.

cloudflare-ai._comment_baseUrl: The account id is part of the URL on purpose, so the whole address is covered by HostAllowlist rather than being appended after that check.

comfyui-local._comment_model: A checkpoint filename your ComfyUI install actually has. WorkflowPath may point at your own workflow exported in API format.

piper-local._comment: VoicesPath is a folder of Piper .onnx voice models; a voice id names a file inside it and may never escape it.

whispercpp-local._comment: ModelsPath is a folder of whisper.cpp ggml .bin weights; Model names one of them by its filename without the extension, and may never escape the folder.

faster-whisper._comment_model: Left unset on purpose: faster-whisper-server transcribes with whichever model it has loaded.

groq-whisper._comment: Shares Groq's service but not its credential: keys are held per provider id, so this one needs its own copy of the key.

Ai._comment_hostAllowlist: Base URLs are operator input, so outbound AI calls are restricted to these hosts. A loopback or private address is only permitted for a provider marked IsLocal.
